title: Birdhouse
description: A birdhouse is a small cedar house with a sloped roof, an entrance hole sized for the intended bird, and no perch, because a perch helps predators reach the nest. The front panel is hinged or screwed for yearly cleaning, the floor has drainage gaps at the corners, and ventilation slots sit under the roof so summer heat escapes. Cedar is left unfinished outside so it weathers naturally, and the house is mounted on a post with a predator guard rather than nailed to a tree that predators climb easily.

Vertical and horizontal slats cross in a grid that vines can grip, the frame is cedar for outdoor life, and the trellis is fixed a few inches off a wall or between posts so air moves behind the plants and the wall stays dry. title: Pergola
description: A pergola is an open garden structure 144 inches long and 120 inches deep, with four six-by-six posts, two beams, eight rafters, and four purlins forming a shaded grid overhead. It is a shade structure, not a roof: rain passes through, vines grow over it, and it is never climbed or loaded with a roof covering it was not designed for. It is the most complex build in this pair, and it needs two builders and a level site.
